workflow_hypothesis: Reentrant finalization re-registers an object during destruction
pattern: Reentrant finalization changes teardown-owned reachability before cleanup completes
description: A teardown path invokes user-controlled finalization while its object, registry links, or related state are still being dismantled. Finalization can either recreate teardown-owned bookkeeping or republish the object through a shared registry; the original cleanup then continues against a topology that has changed underneath it.
precondition: Destruction or teardown invokes user-controlled finalization before all related state and reachability links have been dismantled, and finalization can access that state or its registry.
critical_operation: The cleanup path destroys a value or runs an object finalizer while its surrounding state, ownership records, or registry membership are still in progress.
interference: Reentrant finalization changes reachability during cleanup: it may recreate state already cleared or republish the object in a shared registry while destruction continues.
invalid_assumption: The remaining teardown assumes that finalization cannot add new teardown-owned state or make the object reachable again, so it completes a fixed cleanup sequence or invalidates storage without reconciling those changes.
failure: For recreated bookkeeping, newly reachable state falls outside the cleanup pass and remains leaked; for republished objects, the registry retains a reference to storage that teardown later frees or invalidates, causing a use-after-free or process-terminating failure.
search_strategy: Check whether teardown destroys values or invokes finalizers before all related state and registry links are dismantled.
Check whether finalizers can recreate cleared bookkeeping, containers, ownership records, or other state associated with the teardown context.
Check whether finalizers can retain, resurrect, or re-register the object in a shared lookup or tracking structure.
Verify that cleanup revisits state created during callbacks and that object destruction reconciles renewed registry reachability before freeing storage.
Trace post-teardown registry use for entries whose targets may have been invalidated during reentrant finalization.

evidence.supports: The report shows that destroying a stored value can run user finalization which recreates per-thread bookkeeping during teardown; a fixed clearing sequence then misses the recreated state and leaks it.
The report shows that finalization can re-register the object being destroyed; teardown then frees its storage while the registry still retains the entry, producing later use-after-free behavior.

scope_note: This mixed cluster supports a shared reentrant-teardown pattern with two distinct failure mechanisms: missed cleanup of recreated state and stale or freed storage exposed through renewed registry reachability. It does not claim that every finalizer callback, resurrection, leak, or registry bug follows this sequence.
